obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material, including a series of related unauthorized occurrences across subsidiaries (229.106(a); Item 1.05, Instruction 3)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (POL-03 4.4: disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours of declaration)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date, time, and reasoning of each determination

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05(a); General Instruction B.1 (as amended by Release 33-11216)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination (business days are days the SEC is open)
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact, including on financial condition and results of operations; Inline XBRL (Item 1.05(b))

obligation: SEC Form 8-K/A for information not available at filing
trigger: Item 1.05(a) information was not determined or was unavailable when the 8-K was filed
deadline: Within four business days after the information is determined or becomes available
notify: SEC (amended Form 8-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if the original filing said information was not yet available
clock_starts: Date the information is determined or becomes available
owner: General Counsel (corporate secretary tracks open items)

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); the Attorney General notifies the SEC
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and any material effects of incidents (229.106(b)(2))
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)

obligation: Quarterly disclosure controls evaluation
trigger: Any significant incident during the quarter
deadline: At each fiscal quarter end, with the CEO and CFO; sub-certifications must report the incident
notify: CEO and CFO (certifying officers); audit committee

obligation: Selective disclosure of incident information
trigger: Material nonpublic information about the incident is shared with analysts, investors, or other covered persons
deadline: Public disclosure simultaneously for an intentional disclosure; promptly for an unintentional one
notify: The public (press release or Form 8-K)
owner: Vice President, Investor Relations with the General Counsel

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives, and subsidiary Presidents (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: FTC notification event (Safeguards Rule)
citation: 16 CFR 314.4(j)(1); definition of notification event in 16 CFR 314.2
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted Finance customer information involving at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery. Discovery is the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent of Finance other than the person committing it (314.4(j)(2)); GBS staff running Finance services are treated as Finance's agents
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov: Finance's name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay determination
clock_starts: Discovery by any Finance employee, officer, or agent (including GBS)

obligation: FTC notice: law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days and must include the determination; law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days in writing
notify: FTC (inside the notice)
owner: Finance Information Security Officer with the General Counsel

obligation: Qualified Individual report to Finance's board
trigger: Security events and management's responses are material matters for the report
deadline: In the next annual written report; POL-03 also requires same-day notice to the Finance President
notify: Finance board of directors

obligation: Finance state licensing regulators
citation: State consumer lender licensing laws (six states)
trigger: Incident affecting Finance borrowers or operations
deadline: Per each license state's rules, as listed in counsel's state matrix (not enumerated here)
notify: State financial regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Check each license state with counsel

obligation: Plan sponsor report of a security incident to the group health plan
trigger: The holding company becomes aware of a security incident involving plan ePHI (for example, the benefits site or HRIS benefits data)
deadline: Promptly under the plan documents and POL-03 4.6 (same day); the rule sets no specific deadline
notify: The group health plan (its privacy and security officials) and the TPA

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to individuals (group health plan)
trigger: Breach of unsecured plan PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Affected plan participants and beneficiaries
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if plan PHI is involved; the plan is the covered entity
clock_starts: Discovery by the plan, its workforce, or its agents (164.404(a)(2))

obligation: HIPAA notice to HHS and media (group health plan)
trigger: 500 or more affected (HHS contemporaneously; media if more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction); fewer than 500 logged for HHS
deadline: 500 or more: with individual notice. Fewer than 500: within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS; prominent media outlets
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if plan PHI is involved

obligation: Business associate notice to the plan (TPA, inbound)
trigger: A breach at the TPA or another plan business associate
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after the business associate's discovery
notify: The group health plan

obligation: GBS notice to an affected subsidiary (third-party agent)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (worked example); intercompany services agreement
trigger: Breach of a system GBS maintains for a subsidiary (identity, email, files, HRIS, payment hub, warehouse) involving that subsidiary's personal information
deadline: Statute: as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination. POL-03 4.6: same day
notify: Each affected subsidiary's President and BISO (each subsidiary is the covered entity for its own customers and employees); GBS may send notices on its behalf (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - GBS runs shared systems for every subsidiary

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days); use counsel's matrix and plan to the earliest
notify: Affected residents (employees of any group company; Finance borrowers and applicants; subsidiary customers)
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: State-specific thresholds
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or regulator where required

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: State-specific counts
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example, name with SSN or financial account number with access code)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred; up to 15 additional days if good cause is provided in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each group company for its own Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)

obligation: Florida deemed compliance through federal regulator notice (worked example)
trigger: Notice given under the rules of the entity's primary or functional federal regulator (for example, HHS for the plan's HIPAA notice)
deadline: That notice counts if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the plan - confirm with counsel early; the FTC Safeguards notice goes to the FTC, not to individuals, so it does not replace Finance's individual notices

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the group (vendor, inbound; worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system a vendor maintains for a group company (for example, the outsourced service desk or the HRIS vendor)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The group company (through the SOC and the contract owner)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom or extortion payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Identity takeover, payment fraud, ransomware, or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (supports bank recalls, investigation, and OFAC mitigation)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: Bank fraud notice and payment recall
trigger: Fraudulent or suspicious payment; compromise of a payment hub or bank portal user
deadline: Immediately on suspicion; recall requests are time-critical
notify: Fraud desks of the affected banks; relationship managers

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: use the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline; broker

obligation: Lender and securitization trustee notices
trigger: Events the agreements treat as requiring notice (counsel confirms the covenant wording)
deadline: Per agreement
notify: Administrative agent; securitization trustee

obligation: SL-1 dealer and SL-2 customer notices
citation: SL-1 dealer agreements; SL-2 customer agreements (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting dealer or customer data or service availability
deadline: SL-1: within 72 hours of confirming dealer data is affected. SL-2: within 72 hours of confirming customer data or service is affected
notify: Affected dealers and commercial customers

obligation: Card processor notice
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data at Building Products or Home Services
deadline: Per merchant agreement
notify: Card processor
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data may be involved (payment fields are processor-hosted)

obligation: Federal Reserve computer-security notification incident
trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
notify: Federal Reserve
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a bank holding company (P03 section 1)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
